subject: Urgent: Production latency spike impacting Veridian Commerce - immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@veridian-commerce.com>

Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@veridian-commerce.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden latency spike and increased 5xxs

Dylan,

We're seeing a severe latency spike on the Redwood hosted API impacting our checkout flow starting ~08:45 PT. p95 has jumped from ~120ms to >1.4s and p99 is regularly timing out. We're also seeing ~0.9% 5xx rate and some request timeouts from our end. This is causing failed card tokenizations and customer checkout failures.

Attached is a sample trace and a screenshot of errors from our logs (api_request_trace_20260305.json.gz, error_screenshot_500s.png). Can your team confirm what's happening? This is already affecting revenue. Please escalate.

- Samir

Veridian Commerce

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@veridian-commerce.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@veridian-commerce.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spike and increased 5xxs

Quick findings from initial triage (preliminary):
- Around 08:40 PT we saw a sudden increase in queued requests for the hosted inference pool serving Veridian; queue depth rose from baseline ~120 to ~650 for the model-route serving checkout requests.
- Average batch aggregation dropped (we're seeing more small batches) due to traffic shape changes and upstream clients sending more single-request bursts during peak. That increased per-request overhead and KV cache churn.
- p95 increased to ~1.4s, p99 observed timeouts at ~3s (our request timeout is 4s). 5xxs increased to ~0.9% mostly 524/timeout and some 502s during brief worker restarts.
- When queue depth hit the high watermark our autoscaler briefly cycled a small fraction of workers causing cold starts and increased latencies.

Hypothesis: workload shift produced lots of small, latency-sensitive requests which defeated batching heuristics and increased queueing time; combined with autoscaler oscillation this created a backlog and regression in tail latency.

Immediate recommended mitigations (we've started running these):
1) Temporarily cap queue depth at 250 for the Veridian route to prevent runaway backlog.
2) Reduce max_batch_size from 256 -> 64 for the route to favor faster dispatches.
3) Pin an additional 4 workers to the pool (reduces queue drain time) and disable aggressive autoscaler until stabilization.
4) Enable a short-lived request prioritization policy for checkout RPCs (priority=true) so they get routed ahead of bulk embed jobs.

I'm continuing an analysis of KV cache miss rates and will push flavor-specific logs to the attached trace. Expect a follow-up in ~2 hours with improved metrics and whether we need further remediation.

- Neha
SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spike and increased 5xxs

Ops update and actions we've applied at 11:55 PT: 
- Implemented queue cap (250) on the Veridian checkout route; backlog has started decreasing (queue depth down to ~140 now).
- Reduced max_batch_size to 64 and lowered batching timeout from 30ms -> 12ms to favor faster dispatch.
- Pinned +4 warm workers to the pool; cold starts dropped by ~75% over the last 20 minutes.
- Enabled request-level prioritization for checkout requests.

Early effect: p95 dropped from 1.4s -> ~210ms within 15 minutes; p99 currently ~430ms and still trending down. 5xx rate dropped from ~0.9% -> 0.12%.

Next steps:
- We'll monitor for 4 hours and keep the caps in place while we investigate whether offline batch jobs or new client behavior caused the small-batch pattern.
- If traffic shape doesn't normalize, propose a targeted model-variant with aggressive KV caching (quicker cold-start profile) as a longer-term fix.

I'll post the dashboard link here in 10 minutes with the live graphs.

- Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency spike and increased 5xxs

Samir / Alicia — thank you for the patience and the traces. We deployed immediate mitigations at 11:55 PT (queue cap, smaller max_batch_size, pinned workers, prioritization) and you should see recovery: p95 is improving and errors have dropped significantly. Sean shared early metrics above.

Action items and next steps from Redwood:
- Continue monitoring with us for 4 hours; we'll keep the caps and pinned workers until the traffic stabilizes.
- Our product team will follow up on recommendations to reduce KV cache churn and consider a model-variant for low-latency checkout traffic.
- We'll provide a post-incident summary with timeline, root cause, and suggested configuration changes (by EOD tomorrow).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute post-mortem tomorrow to review mitigations and discuss a long-term SLA/traffic shaping plan.

Apologies again for the disruption — prioritized escalation has been assigned to Marissa (cc'd) for exec-level visibility.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden latency spike and increased 5xxs — customer escalation summary

Summary for leadership — brief: 
- Incident window: 2026-03-05 08:40 PT -> mitigations started 11:55 PT; stabilization by ~12:30 PT.
- Impact: Veridian Commerce experienced p95 regressions and ~0.9% 5xxs; checkout failures impacted revenue.
- Cause (interim): Traffic shape change created many small, latency-sensitive requests; batching heuristics and autoscaler oscillation caused queue backlog and KV cache churn.
- Customer status: Stable; p95/p99 recovered to acceptable levels per Sean's metrics. Customer requested a post-mortem and asked for credits consideration for the outage impact.

Ask for leadership: please advise on credit policy / customer goodwill for this incident (VER-93421). Also approve the post-mortem timeline (EOD tomorrow) and a 30-minute customer review next week.

I'll coordinate the post-incident report and include system traces, timeline, and recommended platform configuration updates (eg. route-level queue caps, prioritized paths for latency-sensitive RPCs, and a low-latency model variant).

- Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
